articles.excerpt: A solicitor who dishonestly created and backdated a letter to the landlord of a vulnerable client has been handed a 12-month suspension, suspended for 24 months.

articles.title: SRA imposes control order on CILEX lawyer who misled lender client
articles.excerpt: A CILEX lawyer who misled her lender client so as to complete a residential property transaction has been made subject to a control order by the SRA.

articles.title: Introducing the Security for Expenses Scheme: a cost-free solution for building owners
articles.excerpt: Security for Expenses arises in the context of building works being carried out by a building owner who shares a party wall with a neighbour.

articles.title: Tomorrow’s legal landscape: helping firms prepare for change
articles.excerpt: Law firms must constantly question the status quo and be willing to adapt. Take nothing for granted. Never say ‘we’ve always done it this way’; never say ‘we’re lawyers and we’re different’.

articles.title: SRA issues £1.5m in fines since enhanced power came on stream
articles.excerpt: The Solicitors Regulation Authority has used the enhanced fining power to issue more than £1.5m fines on solicitors in its first two years, new figures have shown.

articles.title: Blacker fails in challenge to Inner Temple's membership refusal
articles.excerpt: Alan Blacker – the struck-off solicitor once dubbed by a judge as dressing “like something out of Harry Potter” – has failed in a challenge to a decision refusing him membership of the Bar.

articles.title: Junior solicitor struck off for misleading probate clients
articles.excerpt: A recently qualified solicitor at Irwin Mitchell who misled multiple contentious probate clients about the progress of their cases has been struck off.

articles.title: Male barrister disbarred again over harassing female pupils
articles.excerpt: A barrister who won a bid to have his disbarment for sexual harassing two pupils and a woman on a mini-pupillage reconsidered has been disbarred once again.

articles.title: Preparing for an SRA accounts audit: A guide for law firms
articles.excerpt: This guide outlines essential insights for accounts teams to ensure robust compliance and to help audits run smoothly.

articles.title: SRA ordered to pay solicitor £184k costs for "improper" prosecution
articles.excerpt: The SRA has been ordered to pay a solicitor costs of £184,000 over a prosecution the Solicitors Disciplinary Tribunal described as “improperly brought”.

articles.title: £50k fine for lawyer over omissions when applying to join Bar
articles.excerpt: A high-profile Italian lawyer who failed to declare various adverse findings about himself when applying to be called to the English Bar has been reprimanded and fined £50,000.

articles.title: SRA to quiz probate lawyers who “failed to reflect” on training
articles.excerpt: The SRA is to question probate solicitors who “simply listed” in their training records what they had done, rather than providing “evidence of reflection”.

articles.title: Court upholds suspension of barrister in debt to ex-law firm partner
articles.excerpt: The High Court has upheld a six-month suspension imposed on a barrister who failed to comply with a court order to pay £54,600 to a former salaried partner in his law firm.

articles.title: Keystone and NAHL lead way in mixed year for Law PLC
articles.excerpt: Listed legal businesses again proved a mixed bag of investments last year, with Keystone Law and NAHL continuing to go up, the annual Legal Futures analysis of ‘Law PLC’ has revealed.

articles.title: Partners struck off for misleading HM Land Registry
articles.excerpt: Two experienced partners who submitted paperwork to HM Land Registry with fake names to conceal the true owners of properties have been struck off.

articles.title: Post Office investigations to push up costs of barrister regulation
articles.excerpt: The cost of practising as a barrister is set to rise by 8.5%, in part to finance continuing investigations into counsel involved in the Post Office scandal.

articles.title: Law firm defends employment case "entirely of its own making"
articles.excerpt: A solicitor has failed in a claim for a bonus of nearly £10,000 after a contractual dispute an employment tribunal found “entirely” of his law firm’s making.
